subject: art-design

moments.title: Parthenon sculptures
moments.body: Phidias supervises the Parthenon programme, including a colossal gold-and-ivory Athena and the now-dispersed frieze and metopes.
moments.takeaway: Classical Greek sculpture set proportions and poses Western art returned to for two millennia.

moments.title: Polykleitos's Doryphoros
moments.body: The Doryphoros embodies Polykleitos's written 'Canon' on proportion. Only Roman copies survive.
moments.takeaway: We know much classical sculpture only through later copies.

moments.title: Elgin removes the marbles
moments.body: Elgin removes around half the surviving Parthenon sculptures, later sold to the British Museum (1816).
moments.takeaway: The history of a work includes how it left its origin.

now.title: Restitution debates
now.body: Greece has campaigned for the return of the Parthenon marbles since the 1980s. Polychromy research shows ancient sculpture was vividly painted, not white.
now.open_questions: Should universal museums or origin states hold the world's most contested antiquities?

reflection: Our image of 'classical' is a 19th-century reconstruction as much as an ancient reality.
